messages:
incident-bot: Paging: oncall_eng notified for high error rate on /v1/generate from runtime cluster eu-west-1-g. Elevated 5xx (gateway / segfault) starting ~2543219600. Pager: P1. :rotating_light:
Maya Patel: I see the alert, I'm on it — digging into logs now.
Samir Khan: I'm available to help with live mitigation. Do we have a reproducible stacktrace?
Maya Patel: Attaching the top tails from the model-runner logs:
```
2026-03-14T21:27:42Z model-runner[pid=4211]: SIGSEGV at 0x7f8c3b2ff8
2026-03-14T21:27:42Z model-runner[pid=4211]: backtrace: at::native::conv2d -> aten::empty -> mmap -> fatal
2026-03-14T21:27:42Z kernel: Out-of-memory: Kill process 4211 (model-runner) score 987
```
Maya Patel: Pattern: segfault on long seqs + subsequent OOMs, multiple runner instances.
Li Chen: I'm seeing identical crashes in 3 pods across the same GPU host pool. Memory growth looks like KV cache + attention workspace.
Dave Brooks: Correlating with recent kernel-update on that host pool? Any node reboots?
Maya Patel: No infra reboots. Noted that a side-by-side canary that switched to fused attention kernel yesterday.
Samir Khan: Could be a fused kernel regression with large prefix caching. Quick mitigation: enable fallback to non-fused kernel binary and route traffic off the affected hosts.
Priya Nair: Heads up — two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) in eu-west-1 reported timeouts. CS is notifying them.
Maya Patel: Immediate plan: (1) flip routing to fallback model variant (smaller quantized or non-fused kernel) for eu-west-1 for safety, (2) cordon and drain affected nodes, (3) restart model-runner pods after removing fused kernel flag.
Samir Khan: I can push the routing policy change. Command: `rbctl route update --region eu-west-1 --policy fallback-variant --match /v1/generate`
Maya Patel: Doing it now.
incident-bot: Routing policy update started by Samir Khan at 2543219805.
Samir Khan: Done. Traffic % to fallback variant: 100% for eu-west-1. Metrics should show 5xx drop within 30s.
Li Chen: Beginning drain of nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-18 && kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` — repeating for gpu-node-20, gpu-node-21.
Dave Brooks: I'll hold off on reintroducing fused kernel until we reproduce locally. Also capturing a core dump from one crashed runner for analysis: `gcore <pid>` and uploading to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2543219876/
Maya Patel: Observability: error rate down from 18% -> 6% in 2 minutes. Latency still elevated for some clients (timeouts).
Priya Nair: CS: Acme-corp confirmed degraded UX but still receiving responses; Finlytics saw retries and a spike in errors. I've opened tickets and given ETA: mitigation in progress.
Samir Khan: Running a quick smoke test against fallback variant: `curl -X POST https://eu-west-1.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'` -> returns 200 and stream works.
Maya Patel: Good. Next: collect heap profiles and GPU memory stats from affected hosts (nvidia-smi -q, journald). Li, can you capture `pmap`/`smem` from the crashed containers?
Li Chen: On it, uploading to the incident folder. Also found this kernel message repeated before crash:
```
Mar 14 21:26:59 gpu-node-18 kernel: amdgpu: vm_update_mapping failed (-12)
Mar 14 21:27:01 gpu-node-18 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4211 (model-runner)
```
Samir Khan: That looks like mmap failure -> OOM cascade. Might be driver-level frag. For now draining hosts is correct.
Maya Patel: Triage conclusion: fused attention kernel + large sequence KV caching triggers driver mmap fault leading to SIGSEGV and OOM. Impact: multiple customers in eu-west-1, elevated 5xx and timeouts across /v1/generate.
Dave Brooks: Action items for oncall handoff: preserve collected logs and cores (s3 path), keep routing pinned to fallback variant until next patch, keep nodes cordoned. If error rate rises after we re-enable fused kernel, revert immediately.
Maya Patel: Creating follow-up issue for runtime team: include reproduction steps, core dump link, pprof output, and driver/kernel logs.
Samir Khan: I'll also open a canary job to try the fused kernel with instrumentation turned on and shorter sequence lengths to reproduce safely.
Priya Nair: CS note: informed top 5 customers, providing status updates every 30 mins until resolved.
Maya Patel: Escalation? Do we need infra/devices team to look at driver version?
Li Chen: Yes, cc @kernel-ops and @infra-hardware. Driver on these hosts: amdgpu 6.0.2; we have a newer 6.0.4 tested in staging.
Dave Brooks: Tentative mitigation plan for next 24h: (A) keep fallback routing, (B) repro and patch fused kernel codepath, (C) upgrade drivers on drained nodes and run soak, (D) gradually reintroduce nodes under canary.
Maya Patel: I'm going to prepare the post-incident impact summary and timeline. Who's taking the handoff for the night shift?
Samir Khan: I can take primary oncall until 08:00 UTC. Notes for handoff: routing is pinned, drained nodes: gpu-node-18/20/21, core dumps uploaded, tickets opened: RUNTIME-4573, INFRA-982.
Maya Patel: Thanks. Handoff checklist added to the incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident state changed to 'mitigated' at 2543219932 (reduced 5xx to <1% after routing fallback). Oncall: Samir Khan assigned.
Samir Khan: I'll monitor for 2 hours and then start a controlled reintroduce if stable.
Priya Nair: I'll follow up with customer comms and mark impacted customers in the incident ticket.
Maya Patel: Great job team. Final quick note for the postmortem: surface decision rationale for fallback vs autoscale; include cost/latency tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
Samir Khan: copying runbook steps into the ticket for next oncall.
Li Chen: Uploads complete. Core and profiles here: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2543219876/
Dave Brooks: Closing loop with infra to schedule driver upgrade for the drained nodes tomorrow.
Maya Patel: Closing thread—leaving handoff to Samir.
Samir Khan: Acknowledge, monitoring.
